svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.27.2.1 Minimizing and Preventing Ingress and Damage
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.27 CLADDING
Minimizing and Preventing Ingress and Damage
WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except where exterior walls are protected from
precipitation or where it can be shown that
precipitation ingress will not adversely
affect occupant health or safety, exterior
walls are designed and constructed to
(a) minimize the ingress of precipitation into
the assembly, and (b) prevent the ingress of
precipitation into interior space. (See Note
Except where exterior walls are protected from
specific mechanisms of deterioration, such as
mechanical impact and ultraviolet radiation,
exterior walls are designed and constructed to
minimize the likelihood of their required
performance being reduced to an unacceptable
level as a result of those mechanisms.
Subsection 9.27.2. heading carries "(See Note A-9.27.2.)". Drawn: a furred wall with lap siding, arrows schematic.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.27.2.1. (page 9-254)
